title: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider
hookLine: the Provider, of bread and of every other kind of provision

lines: BIRDS LEAVING A TREE AT DAWN.
cards: Early morning: birds leaving a tree. They have no jobs or savings accounts. They don't know where breakfast is.
They just go. And in the evening they come back, and somehow they've eaten. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pointed at exactly that.
Umar reports it, and Tirmidhi records it: if you relied on Allah as He truly should be relied on, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds.
They go out in the morning hungry, and come back in the evening full. Notice one small word: they go out. Today: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider.

teach.b: Ar-Razzaq comes from the root r-z-q; its noun, rizq, means provision, whatever sustains you. Here is Pickthall's translation from Surah adh-Dhariyat: Lo! Allah!
He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unbreakable might. Like ghaffar yesterday, the form razzaq is built for repetition: provision given again and again.

In Surah Hud, there is no creature moving on the earth whose provision isn't upon Allah, and He knows where it rests and where it's kept. The ant, the whale, the baby, the old man. Rizq is wider than bread.
Teachers list other kinds beside food: health, knowledge, friends, a family, work, time, a good night's sleep, and faith itself. Bread is one door into a whole house of provision.

They're provided for, and they still fly out every morning. Muslim scholars read trust in Allah as including effort. Tirmidhi records a man asking whether to tie his camel or trust: tie it, and trust.
That camel gets a day of its own soon. The work is yours; the provision comes from somewhere outside your control. Many Muslims describe that as a weight lifted: not lazier, just less frantic.

This week has been a string of names: the Holy, Peace, the Giver of Safety, the Creator, the Fashioner, the Forgiving, and now the Provider. In the Qur'an's picture, a person is made, shaped, kept safe, forgiven, and fed.

how: Muslims say bismillah before eating and alhamdulillah after, thanking Allah as the Provider; many speak of their income, family and health as rizq, and pair effort with tawakkul, trust, in the spirit of tie your camel and trust.

o: the one who provides for every creature
the one who grants wealth to the faithful
the one who feeds only those who ask

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.
p: every creature's provision is upon Allah

s: rizq means only food and money
scholars include health, knowledge, friends, time and faith.
razzaq and ghaffar share a form built for repetition
both stress again and again: forgiving, providing.
the Qur'an says every moving creature's provision is upon Allah

games.q: the birds in the hadith have no stores and no plan. what do they do each morning?
o: wait in the nest to be fed
go out hungry, and come back full
stay where the food was yesterday
games.why: they go out hungry in the morning and come back full in the evening (Tirmidhi). provided for, and still flying.

practice: Think about the last thing you ate and trace it back, one breath for each link: who cooked or packed it, who drove it to the store, who grew and harvested it, where the rain came from that made it grow.
Then add one other kind of provision in your life right now, a friend, a skill, a quiet hour, and hold both. If you pray, you can say alhamdulillah for them.

wordCard.voice: Ar-Razzaq. The Provider, who gives provision again and again to every creature: bread, and every other kind of rizq. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Provider, again and again; from r-z-q, provision.

carryVoice: Your line: provided for. The birds still go out, and they still come back full. Until tomorrow.
